chain.g: appearance, form, species, kind; apparition; hue, color; beauty; figure of speech

ety.text: From Middle English hewe, from Old English hīew (“appearance, form, species, kind; apparition; hue, color; beauty; figure of speech”), from Proto-West Germanic *hiwi, from Proto-Germanic *hiwją (“hue, form, shape, appearance; mildew”), from Proto-Indo-European *kew-, *ḱew- (“skin, colour of the skin”) or *ḱey- (“grey, dark shade”). Cognate with Swedish hy (“complexion, skin”), Norwegian hy (“fluff, mold, skin”), Icelandic hégómi (“vanity”), Gothic 𐌷𐌹𐍅𐌹 (hiwi, “form, show, appearance”).
From Old French hu or Old French heu, a hunting cry.

senses.d: A color, or shade of color; tint; dye.
The characteristic related to the light frequency that appears in the color, for instance red, yellow, green, cyan, blue or magenta.
ex: In digital arts, HSV color uses hue together with saturation and value.
This puts a completely different hue on the matter.

ety.text: Inherited from Old French, from Latin tincta (“dyed”), from tingere (“to dye”).
From Latin colōrem, from Old Latin colos, from Proto-Indo-European *ḱel- (“to hide, conceal”).
From Latin tincta (“dyed”), perfect passive participle of tingō (“dye”, verb).
From sfumare + -tura. Omitting several steps, from Latin fūmus. For the meaning development compare French nuance (from Latin nūbēs).

chain.g: The stretching or straining of a rope.

ety.text: Probably a semi-learned borrowing from Latin tonus (and influenced by som; compare the Spanish ton, variant of the standard tono, which underwent a similar change, influenced by son, respectively), from Ancient Greek τόνος (tónos, “tone”), from τείνω (teínō, “to stretch”). Cf. also trom, a possible doublet.
